question.problem: Find the projection of the intersection between the elliptic paraboloid $z-4=(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}$ and the plane $x+y=-4$ onto $yz$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
Since we want to find the projection onto the $yz$-plane, we need to eliminate the variable $x.$ First, we solve for $x$ in the equation of the plane, as follows:

$$
x+y=-4\,⟹\,x=-4-y
$$

Substituting the expression for $x$ into the equation of the paraboloid, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}z-4 & =((-4-y)-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} \\ z-4 & =(-y-6)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} \\ z-4 & ={y}^{2}+12y+36+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} \\ z-4 & =\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+12x+36 \\ z-4 & =\frac{3}{2}({y}^{2}+8y+24) \\ z-4 & =\frac{3}{2}(({y}^{2}+8y+16)+8) \\ z-4 & =\frac{3}{2}(y+4)^{2}+12 \\ z & =\frac{3}{2}(y+4)^{2}+16\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection of the intersection is the parabola $z=\frac{3}{2}(y+4)^{2}+16.$
